page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 virtual CPUs (6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled) and 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and supports AVX and AVX512F instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.u1-c1m2.3xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6824.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 15004.59. While small-block cached memory read bandwidth is strong at 640.48 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to 36.23 GB/sec, which is categorized as weak. Similarly, while the instance handles small 135M LLM models adequately, performance on medium 7B LLM models is weak, processing prompts at 23.95 tokens per second and generating text at 8.1 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is appropriate for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose multi-threaded processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.3xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance featuring 12 vCPUs (6 physical cores) powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor and 24.0 GB of memory. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmarks indicate average performance across standard CPU and memory tasks, including a Passmark CPU score of 15004.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6824.0. However, a tradeoff exists in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth and medium-model LLM inference, both of which perform in the lower tier. This instance is suitable for compute-focused workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that require dedicated CPU allocation without high memory density.
